window_alignment.training_window: the D410-S1 shards store frames[t-3..t], four consecutive game frames; one decision = two frames = two renders, so the stack is consecutive

policy_input: none: the action is the recorded teacher tape, the observations are read but never acted on
action_rule: STEP mask = gym_actions.cand_to_mask(tape_candidate, 0); the decision's last STEP frame drops BTN_SHOOT|BTN_BOMB every shoot_pulse_period decisions
referee_state_source: engine STATE reply after each stepped frame

shoot.release_rule: release_due(i, period): last STEP frame of decision i drops BTN_SHOOT|BTN_BOMB

w01c.pin_bypassed_reason: seed10/11 shard sha256 is not in tools/rl/v420_eval_shoot.py's hard-pinned shard set (CLEAR_SHARD_SHA256), so that one assertion was bypassed in order to classify clearability. Nothing else was bypassed: the key-masking, record assembly and validation paths are the tool's own functions, called unmodified and not copied (tape_identity / _run_loop / _assemble_tape_record / validate_tape_record).
w01c.classification_note: pin-bypassed run: classification evidence only. It may NOT be counted as a CONTRACT success/failure source until the shard is registered in the source list or the episode is replayed on an un-bypassed path.
w01c.shard_pin_note: tools/rl/v420_eval_shoot.py pins --replay-tape --shard to the audited clear tape sha256; this driver calls the same functions with a different shard to classify it, and says so here. The only difference from run_tape() is that pin.
